evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: Oracle-bone and bronze component analysis; forms and senses for 事
evidence.text: The database reports that 甲骨文 forms for 事/史/吏/使 were initially one graph, analyzed as a hand holding an object, and later differentiated. It records 事 in bronze inscriptions for duties/official work, events, an office, and in one cited inscription for a verb meaning to send/command; it also gives later transmitted-text examples for matters, undertaking, and serving. The object held is disputed: scholarship cited there proposes a flag, a container for bamboo records, a writing brush, or a hunting implement. These are competing interpretations, not established identifications. Examples include 麥鼎 and 克鼎 for office/duty, 琱生簋 for event, and 小臣守簋 for command/serve.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly database reporting primary inscription evidence
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — oracle-bone component analysis, 又

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: Graphic history and competing interpretations of 史 and related graphs
evidence.text: The database says 史、吏、事、使 were once a single graph, depicting a hand holding something, and became separate graphs. It attributes several rival identifications of the held object: a flag (吳其昌), a container for bamboo slips (王國維), a brush (馬敍倫), or a hunting tool (陳夢家); 徐中舒 proposed a forked hunting implement. It notes graphic differentiation in small-seal forms and cites a proposal that this differentiation occurred around Qin-Han. It also reports oracle-bone uses of 史 for an office/clan/person, matter, and ‘send’; bronze uses include office and uses interchangeable with 事 and 使. This does not establish the object's name or pronunciation, nor that 事 originated as a phonetic loan from a tool name.

evidence.field: Historical attestations and semantic uses of 事
evidence.text: The database cites bronze inscriptions for 事 meaning duty/office, event, and serving/commanding. It cites transmitted early texts for matters/events (including Analects 為政, ‘有事，弟子服其勞’) and for serving/undertaking (Analects 顏回, ‘請事斯語矣’; Xunzi 非相). Its examples distinguish evidence for word senses from the account of graphic development. The site gives inscription names and received-text citations but not exact archaeological dates or a complete textual dating argument; semantic chronology beyond the attested examples remains uncertain.

evidence.field: 說文 and phonological dictionary summary
evidence.text: The page reproduces the Shuowen gloss 職也 (‘office/duty’) and analysis 从史，之省聲, treating 史 as the semantic component and abbreviated 之 as phonetic. This is Xu Shen's historical analysis, not independent proof that the ancient graph was formed that way. The same page gives two Guangyun fanqie spellings, 側吏切 and 鉏吏切, reflecting distinct listed readings, and several reconstruction systems in its summary. Do not merge these with Baxter–Sagart readings.

gaps: The earliest individual attested 事 graph and its archaeological date were not established from inspected glyph images or a primary inscription catalogue; the databases list oracle-bone and bronze categories and selected examples without precise dates.

The held object's identity and name remain disputed. No independent evidence establishes the pronunciation of a depicted flag, writing implement, document container, divination tool, or hunting implement, so a whole-graph phonetic-loan account based on such an object is unsupported here.

The Shuowen explanation 从史，之省聲 is a later lexicographic analysis and conflicts with the paleographic account that 史、吏、事、使 differentiated from an earlier shared graph. Available sources do not settle whether any later component analysis should be called phonetic for the ancient graph.

No independently supported phonetic role for 史 in 事 was established; the similar modern readings cannot prove ancient sound function. No local reading row or external character page for 史 was successfully verified in this session.

Current kMandarin data for 事 was available only as a supplied local row; the official Unicode Unihan record endpoint was attempted and inaccessible. The same is true for 史; no host/component pronunciation comparison was therefore verified through official Unihan records.

No repeatable local extract is recommended: the inspected character-specific paleographic databases provide sufficient concise evidence for this entry, and reuse permissions for a broader extract were not verified.
